name: Union of Concerned Scientists: climate, transport and food (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a tonne of greenhouse gas kept out of the air spares people everywhere, so the result is spread by world population; the small US power-plant and vehicle smoke share is left in the world figure.
summary: The Union of Concerned Scientists' climate and clean energy, clean transportation, food and environment and western states programmes ($37.9M with overhead in the year to September 2025) do technical analysis and advocacy for US climate policy; this model counts the four largest policies it worked on that were won in October 2021 to September 2025 with published tonnes (the Inflation Reduction Act, EPA's 2024 vehicle and power-plant standards and California's Advanced Clean Cars II rule), with its state clean-energy laws and other work as a share. At the defaults a dollar given averts about 0.0059 tonnes of CO₂e (about $170 a tonne), 0.0012 years of healthy life per $1,000, three-quarters of it from the Inflation Reduction Act; it is low because each win is shared with many groups and with what governments would have done anyway (UCS is credited with 1% to 10% of the advocacy behind each), and the federal rules and the law's credits have since been repealed or cut back and California's rule has lost its federal waiver. The biggest uncertainties are the discount rate, the shared years a won reform counts and the deaths per tonne; every branch is discounted for missing data, since no tonne is measured for its work.

rows.explainer: The shared projection of the law's whole cut (facts: climate.ira_tco2e_per_year_2030, Princeton's REPEAT Project) less the larger carbon-capture credit's part (facts: climate.ira_45q_capture_tco2_per_year), which Clean Air Task Force's model counts as its own win: clean power, vehicles, efficiency and the methane programme's grants. rows.label: Evidence adjustment: how far the regulators' and modellers' tonnes should be trusted
rows.explainer: The tonnes are ex-ante estimates by the regulators (EPA, the California Air Resources Board) and modellers (REPEAT), not measured cuts; regulators' estimates of a rule's cuts are sometimes too high (compliance short of the rule) and projections of tax credits have run ahead of what was built. 0.8 (0.5 to 1.1), our judgment, as the Environmental Defense Fund's model for the same kinds of estimate.

rows.label: Other wins of the period not modelled, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: The four branches are UCS's largest climate wins of the period with published tonnes; much of the spending went to others, each a share of the modelled value. California's 2025 laws extending its cap-and-invest programme to 2045 and financing transmission (annual report p. 8): a rough 70 million tonnes a year by the mid-2030s, at about the same shares as Advanced Clean Cars II, about 40%. Maine's 100% clean-power law, Massachusetts' energy law, the Midwest grid operator's $22 billion transmission plan and the PJM grid's battery storage, where UCS was one of several advocates (pp. 8-9), 10%. Fossil-fuel accountability science (attribution research used in the lawsuits of ten states and in the 2025 International Court of Justice and Inter-American Court opinions, pp. 10-11), whose effect on emissions is far off and uncertain, 5%. The Food and Environment programme's farm-conservation, fertilizer and farmworker work beyond the act's conservation money (counted in its tonnes), 5%. 60% (20% to 150%), our judgment, wide because the state laws' tonnes are not estimated here.

source.title: Union of Concerned Scientists, 2025 Annual Report (fiscal year 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2025)

rows.label: Side effect: slower nuclear power from UCS's safety campaigns, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: UCS's nuclear power safety work (inside the climate programme) presses for stricter safety rules and has opposed some new reactor designs and licence extensions; where that slows or closes a reactor, gas and coal fill part of the gap. Since 2018 UCS has also backed policies to keep safe, economic plants running, which cuts the other way. -2% (-10% to 0), our judgment: small beside the clean-power and vehicle wins, and no closure is attributed to it in the period.

rows.formula: (pwr_downstream * pwr_total_adj + veh_downstream * veh_total_adj + ira_downstream * ira_total_adj + accii_downstream * accii_total_adj) / (pwr_downstream + veh_downstream + ira_downstream + accii_downstream)
rows.explainer: The branches' own combined adjustments apply; this is their average, weighted by each branch's expected tonnes before adjustments, for reading only.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.formula: (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + accii_expected_tonnes) / (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + accii_expected_tonnes)
rows.explainer: Every tonne here is fuel burned less near people: power plants, cars and clean power displacing coal and gas (written as the branches' expected tonnes over themselves, as in the Environmental Defense Fund's model).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne of these fuel tonnes, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.formula: (pwr_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_coal_power_smoke_factor + veh_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor + ira_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_power_smoke_factor + accii_expected_tonnes * @climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor) / (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + accii_expected_tonnes)
rows.explainer: Per fuel and place, weighted by expected tonnes: the power-plant standards' tonnes are coal plants' (facts: climate.us_coal_power_smoke_factor), the two vehicle rules' are cars' (climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor), the Inflation Reduction Act's mostly US power's (climate.us_power_smoke_factor), as in the Environmental Defense Fund's model.
